cohort: The study included 86 pregnant rhesus macaques from control groups of investigator-driven pregnancy studies conducted at the Oregon National Primate Research Center.
finding: The study generated a large reference resource of fetal and placental growth demographics, including major organ weights, for use by laboratory animal researchers in future comparative fetal development studies.
cross-section timing: Data compiled across a range of gestational days (G) 50 to G159, with immediate tissue harvesting at delivery.
birth_weight: Fetal growth measures and major organ weights are reported.
